content.value_statement: Architecture choices often grow before requirements are clear. This skill guides context discovery, pattern selection, trade-off analysis, and ADR writing.
actual_capabilities: Prompts users for scale, team, timeline, domain, and constraint details before recommending architecture.
Classifies projects as MVP, SaaS, or enterprise based on size and complexity signals.
Compares data access, domain logic, distributed system, and API patterns.
Guides ADR creation with context, options, decisions, rationale, trade-offs, consequences, and revisit triggers.
Uses examples for MVP e-commerce, SaaS products, and enterprise systems.
limitations: It provides decision support, not validated production architecture.
It depends on accurate project context from the user.
It does not run benchmarks, inspect live infrastructure, or verify runtime constraints.
It gives general examples and may need domain expert review.

use_cases.title: Plan an MVP architecture
use_cases.description: Choose a simple starting architecture that matches a small team, short timeline, and limited scale.

use_cases.title: Document technical decisions
use_cases.description: Create ADRs that explain the chosen option, rejected alternatives, accepted trade-offs, and revisit triggers.

use_cases.title: Compare scaling patterns
use_cases.description: Evaluate modular monoliths, microservices, event-driven design, CQRS, and related patterns against real constraints.

prompt_templates.title: Start an architecture review
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the architecture skill to ask the context questions needed for a new web application. Then suggest a simple first architecture.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new project

prompt_templates.title: Compare pattern options
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare a modular monolith, microservices, and event-driven design for this product: [describe product]. Include trade-offs and revisit triggers.

prompt_templates.title: Draft an ADR
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft an ADR for choosing PostgreSQL over MongoDB for an order management system. Include context, decision, rationale, trade-offs, and consequences.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a migration path
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess our current monolith for future service extraction. Use team size, scaling needs, domain boundaries, risks, and staged migration criteria.

output_examples.input: A solo developer needs an e-commerce MVP in eight weeks.
output_examples.output: Recommendation: start with a monolith, direct ORM access, PostgreSQL, hosted payments, and documented triggers for later extraction.

output_examples.input: A SaaS team needs better boundaries across billing, users, and core workflow.
output_examples.output: Recommendation: use a modular monolith, define module ownership, add repositories where testing matters, and defer microservices.

output_examples.input: An enterprise platform has separate scaling needs across several domains.
output_examples.output: Recommendation: evaluate microservices, API gateway needs, event-driven communication, observability, and distributed transaction risks.

best_practices: Provide constraints before asking for pattern recommendations.
Prefer the simplest pattern that satisfies clear requirements.
Record major decisions as ADRs with revisit triggers.
anti_patterns: Choosing microservices before clear boundaries and scaling needs exist.
Adding repositories, CQRS, or event sourcing for simple CRUD work.
Skipping trade-off documentation for decisions that affect future teams.

faq.question: Does this skill design full production systems?
faq.answer: It supports architectural reasoning and documentation. Final production decisions still need review by engineers who know the system.

faq.question: Can it create ADRs?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes templates for context, decision, rationale, trade-offs, consequences, and revisit triggers.

faq.question: Does it favor simple architectures?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends adding complexity only when requirements and constraints justify it.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is intended for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it inspect my repository automatically?
faq.answer: The skill allows Read, Glob, and Grep guidance. Actual access depends on the host agent and permissions.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it before selecting patterns, splitting services, choosing data access strategies, or documenting a major technical decision.
